identity.description:
Mark D4c done and add the follow-up deliverables D9 to D14

TICKETS.md only: D4c is done, and the follow-ups of the D4c notes become six deliverables. No code change, so no version change.

## Changes

- D4c: a "Done 2026-11-20" block with one line for each experiment and its note.
- "Rules for every experiment after D4c": count the time of a review beside recall, precision and cost; probe 3 to 4 cases across the sizes; report by fixed size limits (under 100, 100 to 300, 300 to 1,000, 1,000 or more); fix the rule before any run. The order: D11 first, D14 beside it, then D9 with D10, D12 after D11, D13 last.
- D9, the verifier: a verifier that rejects more false candidates (it rejects 7 to 9% now), the threshold, the escalation (56% of verifications, $47.81 against $39.99), Opus 5.5 low for speed (4.0 s against 8.0 s median), and the band map of E4 registered before the run. The user's E1 overrides of diff-bugs and history are measured again.
- D10, the severity label: a separate Opus step for each finding (E3b: +0.063, interval 0.000 to +0.111), against labels of Sol at high, best of three.
- D11, the case set: at least 12 new cases from walle and websites, 6 of them at 1,000 changed lines or more, goldens by the pool method. It says how issue 26 relates.
- D12, issue 63: each direction of the issue on the E6 variants, with repeats.
- D13, a tier by PR size: after D11, with more repeats of the small cases first.
- D14, a judge of a second family for the eval (Terra at medium), from the E1 note.
- "Smaller follow-ups found during D4c", and the old follow-up lines that named D4c now point at their outcome or their new ticket.

One critic round checked the text against the notes. Its 15 findings are applied: time and cost terms in each rule, the D12 arm restated for the removal of description-drift, full-set runs in D12, and a person (not a model of either family) as the tie-break of D14.
